title: Low-displacement-rank Mirror layer family
hypothesis: A shared bank of low-displacement-rank generators with small layer codes reconstructs held-out logical dense maps at lower serialized payload and matvec cost than independent dense layers, while matching native LDR controls and native generator/coefficients may erase any Mirror-specific advantage.
physical_object: shared left/right displacement generator banks defining a Toeplitz-like matrix family
mirror_coordinate: per-layer displacement rank and coefficient matrix coding a dense linear operator
logical_multiplicity: 8 task/layer-specific D-by-D maps over one generator bank
controls: native LDR with independently stored generator/coefficients

development.selection_metric: held-out operator NRMSE, full serialized payload bytes, multiply-add proxy and isolated construction/apply wall time

paid_objects: native LDR generator and coefficient payload

success_gate: Across all three audit seeds: held-out operator NRMSE <=1e-5, full payload <=50% independent dense payload at a selected rank, total reconstruction plus apply arithmetic <=1.25x independent dense apply, and strict advantage over byte-near native shared-generator coefficient control. Exact native alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution.
failure_gate: Native shared-generator coefficients exactly reproduce function, payload and compute (Mirror-specific FAIL), or no rank meets preregistered quality/byte/compute gates. Higher-rank byte crossover must be reported.
boundaries: Synthetic linear-operator reconstruction with targets sampled from shared low-rank-displacement generator families; not trained neural-network task quality or capacity.
No GPU/fused-kernel or end-to-end model runtime claim.
Parameter counts are not storage authority; all inference objects are serialized and charged.
